key_insight: A physics-informed CNN-LSTM can forecast long-term photoluminescence degradation of perovskites from early time-series data, generalizing across diverse compositions and crystallinities.
engineering_relevance: This enables faster, cheaper stability screening for perovskite solar materials by reducing reliance on prolonged accelerated-aging experiments.
method: Collected 167 metal halide perovskite samples under heat and light stress
Featurized >86k PL spectra with a physics-informed representation
Trained a hybrid CNN-LSTM to predict future PL intensity for unseen samples
evidence_signal: The abstract reports that the model outperforms baseline benchmarks and generalizes across material groups on a dataset of 167 samples with more than 86k PL spectra.
watch_item: Performance may depend on the quality and representativeness of the physics-based featurization and the stress conditions used during training, so transfer to new protocols should be validated.
paper_title: Physics-informed time-series forecasting of perovskite photoluminescence stability
